samples.summary: Frontend store band tests skip the two sharpest sinks: `colSpan`/`rowSpan` and the `cols` attribute
samples.evidence: The new `describe('bands the numeric attributes a peer can write')` covers exactly five fields — `fontSize`, inline image size, cell `padding`, `rowHeights`, `listLevel`. The same diff rewires two more parses in `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts`: `colSpan/rowSpan` now go through `normalizeTableSpan` (line ~455) and `cols` through `parseColumnWidthsAttr` (line ~475). Nothing in the frontend suite reads a peer-written span or `cols` back through a second store: grepping `colSpan|rowSpan|cols` in that test file finds only the pre-existing `applyCellSpan`/`updateTableAttrs` writer tests (lines 1390, 2863–2906), all with in-band values, which pass whether or not the band is wired. The block comment above the new describe explicitly justifies duplicating these assertions because "the frontend has no `tsc` lane to catch a band wired to the wrong field" — yet the field whose failure is a permanently hung tab for anyone selecting cells in the table (`expandCellRangeForMerges`, the diff's own stated worst case) is the one left uncovered. The docs-package twin (`packages/docs/test/model/numeric-attrs.test.ts`) covers it, but that is a different parser.
searchedFor: read the new 'bands the numeric attributes a peer can write' describe in the diff

samples.summary: `sanitizeDocStyles` is never exercised through either read boundary that calls it
samples.evidence: `sanitizeDocStyles` is the guard the change describes as closing the one string that would "bypass `normalizeFontSize` and `normalizeLineHeight` everywhere at once". It is called from exactly two places: `docsTreeToDocument` (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:329) and `YorkieDocStore.getStyles` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:833). Grepping `sanitizeDocStyles` repo-wide finds tests only in `packages/docs/test/model/named-styles.test.ts`, which calls the pure function directly; grepping `stylesJson` across all test files finds only `packages/frontend/src/components/history/__tests__/snapshot-adapters.test.ts`, whose fixture registry is `{Normal:{fontSize:11,fontFamily:'Arial'}}` — entirely in band and under an unrecognised key, so that assertion passes identically with the sanitize call removed. No test feeds a `stylesJson` containing `{"normal":{"inline":{"fontSize":1e9}}}` through either reader, so a dropped or mis-ordered call at either call site (frontend has no `tsc`) restores the document-wide bypass undetected.
searchedFor: grep stylesJson across repo (test files only match snapshot-adapters fixture)

samples.summary: `MAX_GROUP_DEPTH` and the `staticElements` branch of the slides band have no test
samples.evidence: `bandElementNumerics` caps group recursion at `MAX_GROUP_DEPTH = 32` and `bandLayoutNumerics` walks both `placeholders` and `staticElements`. `packages/slides/test/model/band-numerics.test.ts` — the only unit test file added for this module — tests `bandMasterNumerics` and nothing else; `bandElementNumerics`/`bandLayoutNumerics`/`bandSlidesDocumentNumerics` are only reached indirectly by the frontend store and snapshot-adapter tests, which use a single flat text/shape/table/notes element, one group child (board store), and `placeholders` only. Grepping `staticElements` under packages/frontend/tests returns nothing. The docs twin got an explicit 20 000-deep stack test for its `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH` (`numeric-attrs.test.ts`, 'caps its own recursion instead of blowing the stack'); the slides group chain — whose uncapped walk would `RangeError` inside `read()` and lose the whole deck for the reader, the failure mode the module header names — has no equivalent.

samples.summary: Backend banding is only ever driven through `slides[*].elements`, never through `layouts` or the board body
samples.evidence: `assertValidSlideBlocks` (and therefore `bandSlideBlockNumerics` / `bandSlideCellNumerics` / the inline `fontSize`+image band) is reached from three doors in the controller: slide elements and notes (line 738/742), layout placeholders and static elements via `assertValidLayout` → `assertValidNestedElement` → `assertValidElementData` (line 698/868/1016), and the board body via `assertValidBoardBody` → `assertValidElement` (line 680). Every new band test in both spec files builds its payload with `deckWithTextBody`/`deckWith`, i.e. `slides[0].elements[0].data`, or with `slides[0].notes`. No test puts an out-of-band `fontSize`/`rowSpan`/`columnWidths` inside a layout placeholder or inside a board element, so if the layout or board arm ever stopped routing through the banding walk, the endpoint would store the poisoned deck with no test failing.
searchedFor: read both new describes in docs-content.controller.spec.ts and docs-content.validation.spec.ts (diff)

samples.summary: Three of the four newly normalized `listLevel` call sites (PDF painter, table renderer, peer cursor) have no test
samples.evidence: The diff adds `normalizeListLevel` at `export/pdf-painter.ts:367` and `:593`, `view/table-renderer.ts:525` and `view/peer-cursor.ts:255/395`. `packages/docs/test/model/list-level.test.ts` states outright that these "are left to the unit test of the band itself", and grepping `listLevel` in `packages/docs/test/export/pdf-exporter.test.ts` finds only `listLevel: undefined` (line 345). So only the editor paint pass (`editor-tab-bullet.test.ts`, 'a poisoned list level paints inside the page') and the layout indent are covered; a missed or wrongly-placed normalization at the other three sinks (NaN marker x in an exported PDF, a NaN `Map` key in the table renderer's list counters, an unpaintable peer caret) would ship green.
searchedFor: grep listLevel across packages/docs/test (18 files, none covering pdf-painter/peer-cursor banding)

samples.summary: The `NaN` poison cases in the pagination loops pass without any of this change
samples.evidence: `test('a poisoned font size inside a cell neither hangs nor floods pages')` loops over `[Infinity, 1e9, NaN]` asserting `pages.length <= 202`, and `row-height.test.ts`'s `paginateWith` loops over `[Infinity, 1e9, NaN, -1e9]` with `<= 16`. For the `NaN` (and `-1e9`) inputs the pre-change code produces a `NaN`/non-positive row height, so `while (consumed < rowHeight)` is false on the first evaluation and exactly one page is emitted — the assertion holds with `MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN` and step 5d both removed. The `Infinity` and `1e9` members of the same loops do discriminate, so the tests are not wholly vacuous, but the `NaN` members contribute no signal about the guard they are grouped under (the real NaN claim lives in the separate finite-geometry assertions in `row-height.test.ts` / `table-layout.test.ts`).
searchedFor: read the paginateCellWith / paginateWith loops in the diff
traced `while (consumed < rowHeight)` semantics for NaN in view/pagination.ts

samples.summary: Backend band's column-count cap, `lineHeight` drop branch and `colSpan` are untested
samples.evidence: `bandSlideBlockNumerics` slices `columnWidths` at `MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS` and drops a non-finite `style.lineHeight`; `bandSlideCellNumerics` bands `colSpan` as well as `rowSpan`. The new controller spec exercises `columnWidths: [1e9, -1]` (two entries, so the slice never fires), a clamped `lineHeight: 1e9` (never the delete branch), and `rowSpan: Infinity` only. The docs twin `bandBlockNumerics` has all three covered in `packages/docs/test/model/numeric-attrs.test.ts`, but these are two independent copies of the walk, which is the stated reason the backend copy exists.
searchedFor: read the new 'assertValidSlidesBody bands the numerics' describe in docs-content.controller.spec.ts

samples.summary: Depth-cap boundary untested: only depth 2 (accepted) and 20 000 (refused)
samples.evidence: `describe('the block walks are bounded in depth')` asserts a 20 000-deep body is a 400 and that a 2-deep body is not. Nothing probes near `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH = 32`, so an off-by-one (or a future tightening of the constant) that starts 400-ing bodies a real importer produces would not be caught; equally, a cap accidentally raised to a stack-unsafe value between 33 and ~10 000 would still pass both existing cases.
searchedFor: read OVERFLOW_DEPTH and 'still accepts the nesting a real document reaches' in docs-content.validation.spec.ts

samples.summary: `expect(bandMasterNumerics(junk)).toBe(junk)` is true by the function signature
samples.evidence: `bandMasterNumerics` returns its argument on every path (`return master` in the guard and at the end), so the identity assertion holds regardless of what the function does to the object. The test's only real content is 'it does not throw'; it would pass even if the function mutated `junk` arbitrarily. Asserting `toEqual(structuredClone(junk))` would make the 'untouched' claim real.

verdict.reason: Verified the absence independently. The frontend store routes colSpan/rowSpan through normalizeTableSpan (yorkie-doc-store.ts:460-461) and cols through parseColumnWidthsAttr (:480), but the new band describe (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:3532-3643) asserts only fontSize, image size, cell padding, rowHeights and listLevel. Searching the whole frontend for out-of-band values (Infinity|1e9|NaN), for colSpan|rowSpan in tests/ and src/**/*.test.ts, and for MAX_TABLE_SPAN/MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS/MAX_COLUMN_RATIO/normalizeColumnRatio turned up nothing: the only frontend reads of a peer-written span or cols through a second store are the in-band concurrency assertions (colSpan 2, cols [0.7,0.3]) at yorkie-doc-store-concurrent.integration.ts:770-771, 803-804, 855, 916-920, which pass whether or not the band is wired. The only tests of these two normalizers live in packages/docs/test/model/numeric-attrs.test.ts, a different (non-frontend) parser. Per the band's own doc comment (numeric-attrs.ts:205-211) an unbanded rowSpan hangs expandCellRangeForMerges permanently, so a silently missing/misfielded band on the live editor's read path could ship undetected — major, in-lane missing-test gap.

verdict.reason: Searched repo-wide for the missing coverage and found no counterexample. `sanitizeDocStyles` (packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:190) is called only at packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:329 and packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:833 (readDocStyles, reached from getDocument:808 and getDocStyles:876). The only tests that reach either boundary with a registry are packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.spec.ts:338-365 (readDocsRoot -> docsTreeToDocument, values fontSize 30 / marginTop 40 — all in band) and packages/frontend/src/components/history/__tests__/snapshot-adapters.test.ts:325-341 (fixture registry {Normal:{fontSize:11,fontFamily:'Arial'}} under an unrecognised key, which sanitizeDocStyles passes through verbatim per named-styles.ts:195 and named-styles.test.ts:797). Both assertions hold identically if the sanitize call is deleted, so neither can detect a dropped or mis-ordered call. snapshot-adapters.test.ts:350-353 exercises the `typeof === 'string'` guard, not the sanitizer. Frontend has no test writing root.stylesJson at all (repo-wide grep for stylesJson yields 14 files, only one test file plus its fixture). The sanitizer's own unit tests (named-styles.test.ts:767-820) call the pure function directly. The repo's comparable readers do have store-level band tests (yorkie-slides-store.test.ts:1003-1063, yorkie-board-store.test.ts:397-412), so the docs stylesJson boundary is the outlier; failure of this wiring silently restores a document-wide font-size/line-height bypass, which is major impact.
